scope: AH fixed-prefix search guidance; no implementation or gate

candidate.method: Per-branch reverse directed Dijkstra over exact ordinary edges and locally permitted relaxed via edges; max with the existing TurnLowerBound.
candidate.goalAuthority: Exact per-face branch goal bits, including published tree cells and permitted reached PTH endpoints.
candidate.incomingEdges: Test actual forward predecessor u-to-v; geometry predicates are directed.
candidate.effectBoundary: Router queries mutate caches/work/conflicts. New owner-provided isolated snapshots must preserve live state and effect parity; no production clone API exists yet.
candidate.lifetime: Computed fields are branch-local and invalid after publication or pass/candidate change. Only scratch arrays may be reused.
candidate.queueBoundary: Node heuristic is final and heap priorities are cached. Precompute before seeding, or explicitly reprioritize and reheapify for late activation.
candidate.admissibility: Every actual fixed-prefix route is represented at no greater cost in the relaxed model. A same-face-only bound is invalid while usable via capacity remains.
candidate.unreachableHandling: No production pruning or sentinel behavior is selected by this review.
candidate.activation: No measured early-trigger criterion is established. Unconditional precomputation charges every branch.
candidate.runtimeAccounting: Preprocessing must yield through the existing Session work/deadline boundary; count separately from route expansions without increasing any existing cap.

estimatesOnly.excludedMemory: Router snapshot occupancy, reservations, caches, objects and other existing workspaces.

alternatives.limit: Admissible only once no further via is legal; not a bound for initial witnessed states with remaining via capacity.
Returning its first route changes the existing mixed-face f-cost search order; a separate prepass must honestly share expansion and wall-work budgets.
Unsound because prior via locations affect future legality.

rootClarification: The source audit uses shortest-cost-contract language. This review preserves the existing f-cost ordering as a design choice; it does not claim global optimality is a product acceptance requirement or proved by the current history-omitting state key and first-found quality checks.
nextMeasurement: AI offline lower-bound values on the three already captured graphs; no native frontier was exported, so frontier uplift cannot be measured from these inputs.

subsequentLazyRefreshReview.scope: A local pop-time refresh can avoid global heap mutation/reheapification. This remains a source proof, not native acceptance.
guards: stale best-identity, scope and cap checks precede refresh
same key, g, serial and concrete previous path
replace exact best mapping directly before requeue
return before incrementing expansion or accepting a goal
new nodes immediately use max(old, finite new bound)
fixed branch-local field; no cross-publication reuse
unreachable entries retain old bound, with no pruning
subsequentLazyRefreshReview.accounting: Each refresh consumes existing Session slice work; actual expansion counters and serial allocation stay unchanged. At most one refresh per raised queued node.
subsequentLazyRefreshReview.trigger: 32768 actual branch expansions is a new experimental trigger based on WORK_QUANTUM; runtime benefit and overhead remain unmeasured.
subsequentLazyRefreshReview.limits: Via-history aliasing remains; no global optimality or completeness claim. Native lifecycle, identity, bounds, physical and timing checks remain required.
